proved_step: Let A be a deterministic one-pass transducer on length-N inputs over alphabet Σ, with state set Q, position-dependent transitions δ_i: Q×Σ→Q, and final output h: Q→Y. For any position t, if prefixes u,v∈Σ^t reach the same state, then for every common suffix z∈Σ^(N−t), A(uz)=A(vz). Proof: induct on suffix length k. At k=0 the states agree. If the states agree after k symbols, applying the same position-specific transition δ_(t+k+1) to those states and the same next symbol yields equal next states. Thus final states agree, and h gives equal outputs.

For any Boolean function f on length-N strings, define the residual of a prefix u in {0,1}^t by R_u(z)=f(uz), for z in {0,1}^{N-t}. At layer t let states be the distinct residual functions R_u. For b in {0,1}, define the transition from R_u on b to R_{ub}. This is well-defined: if R_u=R_v, then for every w in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, R_{ub}(w)=f(ubw)=R_u(bw)=R_v(bw)=f(vbw)=R_{vb}(w), so R_{ub}=R_{vb}. At layer N, the residual is the constant f(u), which determines the output. Thus these residual sets and transitions form an exact deterministic layered machine computing f. Moreover, any deterministic exact layered machine has at least as many states at layer t as there are distinct residual functions: prefixes merged into one state must give equal outputs on every common suffix, by induction on suffix length using determinism of each position-specific transition; hence their residuals are identical. This establishes the canonical minimum-state semantic machine, but makes no circuit-cost claim.
